es: Analizar un texto de opinión identificando su tesis, su tono y dos recursos de cautela o persuasión, y citar la frase que lo demuestra.

vocabulary.es: conceder un punto, admitir una razón

teaching.en: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.
teaching.es: Mi tesis es que cada carril para bicicletas del centro debería estar separado físicamente del tráfico, y no solo pintado en la calzada.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis es lo que el autor defiende y suele aparecer pronto: My thesis is… / I will argue that…
segments: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should
be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.
teaching.audioText: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.

teaching.en: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.
teaching.es: Las rutas protegidas pueden animar a familias dudosas a ir en bici, pero la autora presenta ese resultado como una probabilidad y no como una promesa, y hace bien en matizar.
teaching.explanationEs: May es un recurso de cautela: hedge es suavizar una afirmación que no puedes probar del todo.
segments: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome
as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.
teaching.audioText: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.

teaching.en: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.
teaching.es: ¿Acaso algún padre sensato mandaría a un niño en bici junto a camiones pesados? La autora da la respuesta por obvia, y así funciona una pregunta retórica.
teaching.explanationEs: Surely…? no espera respuesta: presenta la idea del autor como evidente y empuja al lector a estar de acuerdo.
segments: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer
treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.
teaching.audioText: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.

teaching.en: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.
teaching.es: Los críticos dicen que el plan es demasiado costoso, así que un autor justo concederá un punto antes de intentar defender el plan en su conjunto.
teaching.explanationEs: Conceder un punto (concede a point) no debilita la tesis: al contrario, hace que el autor suene justo.
segments: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a
point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.
teaching.audioText: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.

teaching.en: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.
teaching.es: Una generalización excesiva como «todo el mundo odia ir en bici» puede sonar firme, pero basta una sola excepción para debilitarla.
teaching.explanationEs: Firm describe el tono; una sweeping statement (con everybody, nobody, always) es un punto débil de un texto.
segments: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound
firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.
teaching.audioText: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.

teaching.en: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.
teaching.es: Los autores que merecen nuestra confianza respaldan sus afirmaciones con pruebas, mientras que los que solo quieren convencernos suelen apoyarse en la emoción.
teaching.explanationEs: Back up = respaldar con pruebas; persuade = convencer, a menudo con emoción además de datos.
segments: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas
those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.
teaching.audioText: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.

prompt.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la tesis de la autora.

choices.text: Museums should charge no entrance fee, because fees keep out those who benefit most.
Museums should stay free only for children, because adults can afford the price.
Museums should raise their entrance fee, because galleries are short of money.

feedback.es: La tesis aparece tras «I will argue that»: una entrada de pago deja fuera a quienes más ganarían con la visita. Las otras opciones cambian el alcance o recogen la postura de los críticos.

hint.es: La tesis suele anunciarse con una fórmula como «I will argue that».

origin.text: Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.

prompt.es: Elige qué función cumple esta pregunta dentro del texto.

choices.text: It genuinely asks readers to decide whether the evidence is convincing.
It presents the writer's view as obvious, inviting the reader to agree.
It admits that the evidence for the writer's claim is very weak.

feedback.es: Es una pregunta retórica: no espera respuesta ni pide al lector que valore las pruebas; da por obvia la tesis y empuja al lector a coincidir con ella.

hint.es: Fíjate en que nadie necesita contestar la pregunta: la respuesta ya está dada.

origin.text: Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it?

prompt.es: Completa: «Los resultados podrían animar a otros municipios a probar la idea.»

feedback.es: Might, may o could suavizan la predicción: la autora admite que los datos de una sola ciudad no permiten asegurar el efecto.

hint.es: Es un verbo modal que expresa posibilidad, no certeza.

origin.text: The figures come from one city only. The results ___ encourage other councils to try the idea, but more data would help.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué prueba usa la autora para respaldar su tesis?

choices.text: Donations to the capital's main museum doubled once the charge was dropped.
Most parents in the capital said they would visit more often.
Visits to the capital's main museum doubled once the charge was dropped.

feedback.es: La prueba es un dato concreto de la capital: las visitas se duplicaron en un año sin entrada. Las donaciones solo subieron (no se duplicaron) y no hay encuesta a padres.

origin.text: Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué tono predomina.

choices.text: Personal and firm, though ready to accept that the cost is real.
Bitter and sarcastic, convinced that councils will never take the problem seriously.
Detached and analytical, weighing the cost of the scheme without sharing any personal story.

feedback.es: El hablante cuenta una experiencia propia (la furgoneta), defiende su idea con firmeza y reconoce que el costo es real: firme pero dispuesto a conceder, ni amargo ni distante.

origin.audio: I have cycled to work for twelve years, and I can tell you that paint is not safety. Last spring a van clipped me in a lane that the council proudly called safe. I am not saying that every road needs a concrete wall, and I accept that the cost is real. But surely a child on a bicycle deserves more than a white line? If councils want more people to cycle, they must first make it feel safe.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el recurso que usa el autor.

pairs: Admittedly, the scheme is not cheap.
Visits doubled in the first year alone.
It would seem that the trial has worked.
Surely no one wants to see it close?

feedback.es: Admittedly reconoce un punto contrario, la cifra es una prueba, it would seem limita la afirmación y surely…? da la respuesta por obvia.

pairs: Admittedly, the scheme is not cheap.
Visits doubled in the first year alone.
It would seem that the trial has worked.
Surely no one wants to see it close?

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor ante quienes critican el trabajo remoto?

choices.text: He rejects their worry out of hand and argues that offices no longer matter at all.
He takes their worry seriously but thinks it is a poor reason for a fixed rule.
He shares their worry but believes that the evidence is still too weak to decide.

feedback.es: Admite que algunos empleados pueden rendir menos, pero concluye que eso no justifica imponer cinco días de oficina: toma en serio la objeción sin aceptarla como regla.

origin.text: Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Yet the largest study on the subject, covering some ten thousand workers, found that work stayed just as good, while far fewer people quit their jobs. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. Even so, insisting on five days a week seems to me a habit rather than a strategy, and it may cost companies their best people.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe «I am not saying that the office is useless»?

choices.text: To step back from his thesis and accept that offices are still necessary.
To reassure managers that employees will still work well from home.
To deal with an objection early and keep his argument fair.

feedback.es: Se adelanta a una objeción («entonces, ¿la oficina no sirve?») y limita su tesis para que siga siendo creíble; no retrocede en ella ni busca tranquilizar a los jefes sobre el rendimiento.

origin.text: Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Yet the largest study on the subject, covering some ten thousand workers, found that work stayed just as good, while far fewer people quit their jobs. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. Even so, insisting on five days a week seems to me a habit rather than a strategy, and it may cost companies their best people.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento de la reunión: ¿qué da a entender la directora?

choices.text: She is ready to approve the proposal, but only after a smaller trial.
She likes the detail but thinks another team should run the project.
She backs the proposal fully and considers the timeline perfectly realistic.

feedback.es: Elogia la propuesta, duda del calendario y propone un piloto más pequeño: apoya la idea con condiciones; no pide que otro equipo la dirija ni la aprueba sin reservas.

origin.audio: I have read the proposal twice, and I have to say that it is detailed. However, I cannot help wondering whether the timeline is realistic, given that the team is already stretched. I would be happy to support it, provided we agree a few conditions first. Perhaps we could start with a smaller pilot and review the results in the spring?

prompt.es: Completa: «La autora concede un punto, pero insiste en que no hacer nada costaría más.»

feedback.es: Concede a point es la colocación para reconocer que los críticos tienen parte de razón antes de defender la propia tesis.

origin.text: Critics say that the scheme is too expensive. The writer is happy to ___ a point, but she insists that doing nothing would cost more.

prompt.es: Elige la descripción más exacta del tono del autor.

choices.text: Bitter and angry, blaming the council for ignoring residents.
Disappointed but measured, acknowledging the council's difficulty.
Resigned and cold, accepting the cuts as necessary.

feedback.es: Se declara decepcionado, pero reconoce la presión del municipio (I do see the pressure) y pide una alternativa: tono mesurado, no rencoroso ni indiferente.

origin.text: The new bus timetable starts next week. To be honest, I am disappointed: buses will run half as often, although the town is growing. The council says that savings were necessary, and I do see the pressure it is under. Still, fewer buses will leave older residents stranded at home. Surely there is a fairer way to balance the books?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo sostiene su tesis la hablante.

choices.text: Teenagers already eat well, so cooking lessons would add very little.
Cooking matters, but schools should wait until proper kitchens have been built.
Cooking deserves a place in the timetable, despite the cost involved.

feedback.es: Acepta que el horario está lleno y que las cocinas son caras, pero mantiene que cocinar es una habilidad vital: defiende la tesis reconociendo el costo.

origin.audio: In my opinion, every school should teach cooking. I know that timetables are already crowded, and I accept that kitchens are expensive to build. Yet cooking is a life skill, and it may well improve how teenagers eat. Why would we leave something so important to chance?

prompt.es: Completa: «Los autores matizan con prudencia sus resultados.»

feedback.es: Hedge es suavizar una afirmación con expresiones de cautela (suggests, appears) cuando no hay pruebas definitivas.

origin.text: Nobody can be certain yet. The authors carefully ___ their findings with words like suggests and appears, instead of claiming proof.
